payload.content:
The Bachelor of Science in Horticulture at UAEU provides students with fundamental scientific knowledge on the production and protection of horticultural plants in arid environments, develops skills for resource-efficient cultivation, and enhances abilities to sustain natural resources and improve environmental quality.

The program combines theoretical knowledge with practical training in research labs, experimental farms, and internships, preparing students to be creative experts in areas such as organic farming, plant protection, greenhouse management, landscaping, and applied biotechnology.

Students complete required courses totaling 45 credit hours covering topics like soil and water principles, plant protection, horticulture introduction, plant physiology, irrigation management, and a senior project.

The Bachelor of Science in Horticulture is offered by the College of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine, Department of Integrative Agriculture, as an undergraduate degree program.
